Give AI your buyers' questions and it shows you which buying moment you're missing from.

We've published our first AI Shortlist study. Six AI engines, 309 UK questions about smart trainers, apps and smart bikes, 5,562 answers.

The finding I'd put in front of any brand team is where the answers come from. Editorial cycling media supplied over half the citations, led by BikeRadar, Cyclingnews and Cycling Weekly. Reddit, YouTube and forums supplied 3% to 5%.

So the buyer's guide review now does two jobs. The rider reads it and the engine quotes it.

For transparency, I've worked with Wahoo and Wattbike, was on the founding team at RGT and work with Ribble, which isn't ranked. The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The interactive report, episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/which-indoor-cycling-brands-does-ai-recommend/
clips.text: Where does the AI get all this from? Mostly cycling media. Editorial sites supplied between fifty-one and fifty-six per cent of the citations, led by BikeRadar, Cyclingnews and Cycling Weekly. Reddit, YouTube and forums supplied three to five per cent. The exception is apps, where the brands' own websites carried thirty per cent of the citations. When we covered the citation moving off the page back in June, the argument was that rankings had stopped predicting who AI quotes. This is what that looks like in one category. The buyer's guide review on BikeRadar now does two jobs. The rider reads it, and the engine quotes it. So the work for most brands is earned media, not just their own pages.

clips.linkedin:
Give AI your buyers' questions and it shows you which buying moment you're missing from.

In our AI Shortlist study of UK indoor cycling, the leader changed with the question. Rouvy won scenery questions, MyWhoosh won value and TrainerRoad won performance training. The engines disagreed on challenger brands too.

So start by having AI map your buying moments. Give it your search queries and customer service tags, and it returns the questions buyers ask most, tagged by moment.

Then check each engine separately. Ask the same questions three times on each and track how often you're named, because one answer tells you very little.

For transparency, I've worked with Wahoo and Wattbike, was on the founding team at RGT and work with Ribble, which isn't ranked. The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The prompts, report and episode are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/which-indoor-cycling-brands-does-ai-recommend/
clips.text: First, get your AI to map your buying moments. The five questions a buyer in your category asks most, tagged by moment, value, beginner, performance, problem. Give it your search queries and your customer service tags, and it hands you the list with the moment you most need to win at the top. Second, check each engine separately. Your position on one says very little about the others. Set it up as a routine. Run the same questions three times on each engine, record which brands each answer names, and track how often you appear, because a single answer tells you very little.
